content.text:
Clattertrap rules v1

World
- Units are centimetres and degrees. The origin is bottom-left, x runs right, y runs up. A part's position is its centre unless the table says otherwise.
- Angles are counterclockwise positive. angle_deg 0 is horizontal; a beam at -15 slopes down to the right.
- Gravity is 981 cm/s^2 downward. Everything starts at rest and physics starts at once, so anything in the air falls.
- The floor is solid. There are no walls and no ceiling: a part whose centre goes more than 50 cm outside the level rectangle is removed.
- Time advances in steps of 1/120 s. A run ends when the goal is met, when the level's time limit passes, or when everything has stopped moving.

Materials
| material | mass of a ball | bounce | friction |
| steel | 1.00 kg | 0.2 | 0.2 |
| wood | 0.15 kg | 0.3 | 0.5 |
| rubber | 0.20 kg | 0.8 | 0.9 |
Bounce between two bodies is the larger of the pair; friction is the average. Beams, dominoes, crates, seesaws, and buckets are wood.

Parts you may place
The level's inventory says how many of each kind. Kinds it does not list are not available.
| kind | fields | size | behaviour |
| beam | x_cm, y_cm, length_cm (20..150), angle_deg | 4 cm thick | fixed wood plank |
| funnel | x_cm, y_cm (throat centre), mouth_cm (30..150), throat_cm (14..mouth), height_cm (20..80) | 2 cm walls | fixed; two walls slope in from the mouth down to the throat |
| ball | x_cm, y_cm, material (steel, wood, rubber) | radius 6 cm | rolls and bounces as its material does |
| domino | x_cm, y_cm, angle_deg (default 0) | 4 by 20 cm | wood tile standing on end; tips when pushed |
| crate | x_cm, y_cm, side_cm (10..40) | square | wood box |
| seesaw | x_cm, y_cm, length_cm (40..150), angle_deg (default 0) | 4 cm thick | wood plank that pivots freely about its centre, which is fixed in space |
| pendulum | x_cm, y_cm (the pin), length_cm (20..120), angle_deg (default 0, measured from straight down) | steel weight of radius 5 cm | swings on a rigid rope from the pin and is released at once |
| spring_pad | x_cm, y_cm, angle_deg (default 0) | 30 by 4 cm | fixed plate; a body that lands on it gets a kick of 0.6 N s along the plate's normal: a wood ball leaves at 4.1 m/s and rises about 85 cm, a steel ball at 0.6 m/s rises 2 cm |
| bucket | x_cm, y_cm (centre of the floor's underside), width_cm (15..60), height_cm (15..60) | 2 cm walls | wood open box; it can move |
| balloon | x_cm, y_cm | radius 10 cm | rises at up to 1.5 m/s and slides along the underside of anything above it; a pin pops it |
| pin | x_cm, y_cm (the base), angle_deg (default -90, pointing down) | 1 by 16 cm | fixed needle |
| rope | a, b, max_length_cm (10..200) | no body | ties the centres of parts a and b; slack until taut, then keeps them within that length |

Goal objects and fixtures only a level places
| bell | brass disc of radius 10 cm hung below its anchor | rings when hit hard enough: a wood ball at 1.4 m/s or a steel ball at 0.2 m/s; only a moving part rings it, never a beam or another fixed part |
| button | 12 by 3 cm cap on a spring | pressed when pushed down its full travel and held there |
| basket | open box with 2 cm walls | counts objects that come to rest inside it |
| portal | two ends, orange and blue, each 30 cm across, facing the way its angle_deg points | a ball that enters either end comes out of the other at the same speed, heading out the way that end faces, so a ball dropping into an end set in the floor leaves an end set in a wall sideways; nothing but a ball passes; a portal can be a via waypoint |

Goals
ring, press, fill (count objects at rest inside the basket), or pop. A goal may list via: part ids that must be touched in that order before the goal counts. The waypoints and the goal must be the work of one chain of parts that have touched each other since the start; a part that moves on its own and never meets that chain does not count, and neither do objects it leaves in the basket. When the level has moving fixtures, such as its ball, the chain that meets the goal must include one of them.

Placement rules
- Every placed part's centre must lie inside a build zone. Fixed objects are exempt.
- Nothing may overlap at the start: not another part, a fixed object, or the floor. Leave a gap of a few millimetres.
- Every part has a unique id; the fixed objects' ids are taken.
- Lengths outside the ranges above are rejected. check lists every problem with its JSON path and a fix.

Scene JSON
{"level": "<level id>", "parts": [{"id": "example", "kind": "beam", "x_cm": 120, "y_cm": 210, "length_cm": 120, "angle_deg": -15}]}
Field names carry their units. The full schema: clattertrap rules --schema

portal-jump: Through the portal (tier 5)
Goal: ring bell after touching post, then portal.
Time limit: 20 s. World: 400 by 300 cm.

A steel ball hangs in the air at (40, 280), top left, and falls from the start. A portal has two ends: an orange end set in the floor at (275, 3), facing up, and a blue end set in the left wall at (10, 280), facing right. A ball that enters either end comes out of the other at the same speed, heading out the way that end faces: a ball dropping into the orange end leaves the blue end moving right, and its sideways speed on arrival becomes rise or fall on the way out. A short fixed beam, the post, runs level from x = 150 to x = 190 with its top at y = 162. A bell hangs at (340, 220), high on the right, inside a fixed box that is open only on its left side: a roof from x = 300 to x = 370 at y = 250, a shelf at y = 190, and a wall at x = 370 between them. The bell's bracket is 20 cm above it. The build zone covers x from 20 to 300 at every height. The ball has to touch the post, then pass through the portal, and then come in through the open side of the box and ring the bell. Chain length is scored too.

Fixed objects:
  ball0: steel ball at (40, 280)
  portal: portal: orange end at (275, 3) facing 90 deg, blue end at (10, 280) facing 0 deg
  post: beam 40 cm long centred at (170, 160), angle 0 deg
  roof: beam 70 cm long centred at (335, 250), angle 0 deg
  shelf: beam 70 cm long centred at (335, 190), angle 0 deg
  back: beam 60 cm long centred at (370, 220), angle 90 deg
  bell: bell at (340, 220), hung 20 cm below its anchor
Build zones: x 20..300, y 10..290
Inventory: beam 6, funnel 1, ball 1, domino 4, crate 1, seesaw 1, spring_pad 1
Showcase level: chain length is scored too.

text:
I'll read the physics before building anything. Clattertrap's rules are the primary source, so I'll start from there.

Key facts from the rules and level:
- Ball0 is steel, starts at rest at (40,280), and can't gain energy from falling. The fastest it can reach the orange end is about 737 cm/s.
- Ringing the bell from the open side needs roughly 800–850 cm/s through the blue exit, or a bounce off a beam that redirects it into the box window.
- Plan: ball0 rolls down a ramp, grazes the post, falls into the orange end, exits blue moving right, bounces off a short beam, and drops into the window to hit the bell.

I'll write a first scene with two beams and validate it.
The layout matches the plan: the ramp runs from about (30,270) down to (140,205), the post sits below its end, and BM2 sits over the portal's exit path. Running it.

text:
I submitted a machine that does not meet the goal. It touches the post and passes the portal, but it never rings the bell.

**Submitted scene:** a ramp (beam `r1`, centre (85, 237.5), 128 cm, −30.6°), a bounce beam (`bm2`, centre (205, 218), 50 cm, level), and a funnel (`fun`) with its throat at (275, 22), mouth 150 cm, throat 30 cm, height 80 cm.

**What happened in the final run (goal not met, 20 s time limit):**
- Ball0 rolled off the ramp and touched the post at 1.04 s, which counts as "via post".
- It dropped into the funnel and through the orange end at 1.94 s, which counts as "via portal".
- It came out of the blue end with too little speed to reach the bell. It fell back onto the ramp and then looped between the blue exit, the ramp, the post and the funnel for the rest of the run.

**Why the bell was out of reach:**
- Ball0 is steel and starts at rest, so it can't carry more energy than a fall from 280 cm allows. Losses on the post bounce and inside the funnel took most of that.
- The bell window at x≈300 needs the ball moving at roughly 550–850 cm/s out of the blue end. Ball0 left at a fraction of that.
- Without the funnel the ball missed the orange end, so the funnel was needed to catch it. Its bounces cost too much speed.

**Runs:** 7 of 8 used. The submission was the eighth; I didn't use its result to adjust, so the final run is the submitted scene's own result.

**What I'd try next:** a way to keep more of ball0's energy through the post and funnel, such as a graze on the post top with less bounce loss, or a funnel with fewer wall contacts. Either would need more runs than I had.
